name: Homer Searches for Dr. Larch
description: Homer enters from the corridor calling out for Dr. Larch, his voice urgent as he moves through the hall.
related_events: Homer calls out for Dr. Larch in the corridor

name: Larch and the Nurses Say Goodbye to Homer at the Door
description: Larch and the nurses stand at the front door, waving and calling goodbye to Homer as he departs. Once he is gone, they close the door.
related_events: Larch and nurses bid farewell to Homer at the front door

name: Larch Closes the Door on the Operating Room
description: Dr. Larch steps into the hallway and quickly pulls the operating room door shut behind him, the latch clicking into place just as Homer approaches. The movement is sharp and deliberate, cutting off the view of the room's interior. Inside, a figure lies on the table, still and pale under the bright lights. Larch stands in front of the door for a moment, his back to it, then turns to face Homer with a calm expression.
related_events: Larch closes door to hide abortion patient from Homer

name: Larch Carries Homer to St. Cloud's
description: Dr. Larch carries Homer up the hill toward St. Cloud's orphanage. The two move slowly in the quiet air, the building coming into view as they climb. Larch holds the child securely, stepping carefully on the path leading to the orphanage doors.
related_events: Larch carries Homer up the orphanage hill

name: Nurse Edna Leads Evening Prayers in the Bunk Room
description: In the dimly lit bunk room, Nurse Edna stands among the beds, reciting prayers aloud. The girls lie on their mattresses, their hands pressed together on their chests, their eyes closed as they listen and silently pray along with her.
related_events: Nurse Edna leads girls in evening prayers

name: Hazel Walks Across the Snowy Lawn with Her New Parents
description: Hazel steps off the porch of the orphanage and walks across the snowy lawn, flanked by her new parents. Behind her, the orphans stand at the windows, watching in silence as she moves away from the building and toward the gate.
related_events: Hazel walks across snowy lawn with new parents

name: Homer Assists Larch in Delivering a Baby
description: Homer stands beside Dr. Larch in the hospital delivery room, helping as the doctor guides the baby through the birth process. He hands over instruments, supports the mother when instructed, and watches as the infant is safely delivered into Larch's hands. The baby cries, and Larch places it on the mother's chest.
related_events: Homer helps Larch deliver a baby

name: Larch Rescues Homer from Abusive Foster Parents
description: Larch bursts into the home of the second couple and finds Homer in bed, crying and covered in bruises. Without hesitation, he lifts Homer from the bed and holds him, then turns a furious gaze toward the couple.
related_events: Larch rescues Homer from abusive couple
Larch discovers Homer has been beaten

name: Edna and the Girls Say Goodbye to Hazel
description: Edna, standing with the girls, offers a farewell blessing to Hazel, saying they should be happy for her because she has found a family. The girls then call out together, 'Good night, Hazel!' in unison, repeating it once more before falling silent.
related_events: Edna and the girls bid farewell to Hazel

name: Larch Explains Record Destruction to Adoptive Couple
description: Dr. Larch stands in his office with a couple who are adopting Hazel. He tells them that he destroys all records identifying the natural mothers of orphans. He says the reason is for the orphans' sake. He explains that while the children will one day want to know about their past, they should focus on their futures instead of looking back.
related_events: Larch delivers lecture on orphan record destruction

name: Edna and Angela Chase the Children
description: Two nurses, Edna and Angela, chase children through the halls of St. Cloud's in the early morning. The children run ahead, scattering up the stairs, while the nurses follow closely behind. The sound of footsteps and distant voices fills the building as the day begins.
related_events: Nurses Edna and Angela chase children during morning routine

name: The Couple Returns Homer at Night
description: The door swings open again under the dim light of another night. The same couple steps through, guiding Homer with them. Their faces are tense, eyes drawn with worry. Nurse Edna stands in the doorway, then steps aside to let them pass into the facility.
related_events: Couple returns Homer to the facility
Nurse Edna admits the couple and Homer

name: Homer Listens to the Fetal Heartbeat
description: A very pregnant woman lies on the examination table, her bare belly exposed. A small hand enters, placing a stethoscope gently on the curve of her abdomen. Young Homer rises into view, the stethoscope around his neck, his eyes closed in concentration as he listens. Behind him, Larch appears in the doorway, pausing at the sight. He watches silently, then offers a faint smile before remaining still, observing.
related_events: Homer listens to unborn child's heartbeat with stethoscope
Larch observes Homer and smiles faintly

name: Orphans Run to the Lawn After the Front Door Opens
description: The front door opens. The orphans run outside onto the green lawn.
related_events: Front door opens
Orphans run outside onto the green lawn

name: Homer Feels the Fetus Kick
description: Dr. Larch examines a pregnant woman. He calls Homer over and places the boy's hand on the woman's abdomen so he can feel the fetus moving inside.
related_events: Dr. Larch examines pregnant woman
Dr. Larch guides Homer's hand to feel fetus movement

name: Homer Arrives at the Third Family's Home
description: The door opens to a third couple who smile warmly and embrace sixteen-year-old Homer as he arrives. Behind them stands their daughter, an attractive girl a little older than Homer. As they welcome him inside, Larch's voice is heard, recalling his words to the family: to take good care of Homer, because he was a special boy.
related_events: Third couple welcomes and embraces sixteen-year-old Homer
Larch gives instructions to third family about caring for Homer

name: Couple Enters St. Cloud's Orphanage
description: A man and woman approach the main entrance of a large brick building and step inside. The sound of crying babies fills the air as they cross the threshold. Inside, the walls are plain, the floors worn, and the air carries the faint scent of antiseptic. A distant door creaks shut, and a nurse passes down the hall without speaking to them.
related_events: Couple enters the orphanage building

name: The Train Arrives and Departs at St. Cloud's Station
description: On an overcast morning, snow covers the cracked platform of a rundown train station. A train rolls in slowly, its brakes hissing as it comes to a stop. After a brief pause, the train pulls away, leaving the station empty once more. Behind the platform, the orphanage at the top of the hill looms in the distance.
related_events: Train arrives at rundown station on overcast morning
Train departs from snowy station platform

name: Edna Leads a Prayer in the Bunk Room
description: In the bunk room, Edna prays aloud, asking for mercy, safe lodging, holy rest, and peace. When she finishes, all the girls respond together, saying 'Amen! Amen! Amen!'
related_events: Edna leads a prayer for safe lodging and peace
The girls collectively respond to the prayer with affirmation

name: Homer Leaves with His Suitcase and Looks Up at the Stepsister
description: Homer walks out of the house carrying his suitcase. From her window, the stepsister watches him. He makes his way to the street and looks up toward her. She remains at the window, looking down as he stands there for a moment before continuing on.
related_events: Homer leaves the house carrying his suitcase
Stepsister observes Homer's departure from the window
Homer looks up at the stepsister from the street

name: Larch and Homer Respond to New Patients
description: Dr. Larch wakes up and shakes off the lingering effects of ether. Homer enters and tells him there are two new patients, one of whom needs delivery. Dr. Larch and Homer leave together to attend to them.
related_events: Larch wakes up and recovers from ether daze
Homer informs Larch about new patients
Dr. Larch and Homer depart together

name: Dr. Larch Presents Homer to Adoptive Parents and Shares the Story of His Name
description: In Dr. Larch's office, he holds the infant Homer and shows him to the adopting couple. He hands the baby to the parents, who look at him with pride. Dr. Larch tells them he named the child after the Greek writer Homer, and added 'Wells' because the boy seemed very deep. The couple nods hesitantly. A voiceover then reveals that the name was actually chosen by Nurse Angela—'Homer' after one of her family's many cats, and 'Wells' in memory of her father, who drilled wells for a living.
related_events: Dr. Larch presents infant Homer to adopting couple
Dr. Larch reveals origin of infant's name
Adopting parents accept infant Homer
Dr. Larch discloses origin of Homer's name through voiceover

name: Larch Instructs Homer to Be of Use at St. Cloud's
description: Homer stands by the window, gazing outside as Dr. Larch speaks to him. Noticing Homer's inattention, Larch tells him that if he intends to remain at St. Cloud's, he must contribute and be of use.
related_events: Homer looks out the window while being instructed
Larch instructs Homer to be of use at St. Cloud's

name: Parents Find Homer and Stepsister in Bed
description: The parents burst into the room and find Homer and the stepsister in bed together. The father immediately lunges at Homer, who scrambles up and runs around the bed, dodging him. Across the room, the mother grabs her daughter and begins striking her. The daughter curls up and pulls a pillow over her body, trying to block the blows.
related_events: Parents discover Homer and stepsister in bed together
Father chases Homer around the bed
Mother beats her daughter who covers herself with a pillow

name: Carla Walks Away from St. Cloud's Sobbing
description: Carla descends the hill away from the St. Cloud's building, moving in silence with tears streaming down her face. She does not look back as the silhouette of the building stands against the sky, and the sound of her quiet sobs blends with the hush of the evening.
related_events: Carla walks away from St. Cloud's building while sobbing

name: Edna's Off-Screen Reflection
description: Edna's voice carries from beyond the scene, reciting words about shadows lengthening, the evening settling in, the world growing quiet, and the fever of life subsiding. The sound of her voice lingers as Carla walks down the hill away from St. Cloud's, her figure silhouetted against the sky, weeping, not looking back.
related_events: Edna recites a reflective monologue off-screen

name: Angela Sings Larch Awake
description: Angela sings along to the phonograph, her voice pulling Larch from his drowsy state. He stirs, grumpy and disoriented, but she leans close and sings into his ear, holding the ether cone just out of his reach. He turns away, but she tickles him and gently bites his ear, drawing him back. He tells her he was dreaming of her, how beautiful she was. She slips from his arms and says he wasn’t dreaming of her. He insists he was. She replies that then she wasn’t beautiful. He protests, saying she was, she is, and that the dream was fantastic. She smiles and tells him it was just the ether, Wilbur.
related_events: Angela sings along to phonograph music, rousing Larch from ether-induced drowsiness
Angela teases Larch by withholding the ether cone and tickling him

name: Angela Teases Larch After His Dream Confession
description: Larch wakes from his ether-induced sleep and tells Angela he dreamed of her beauty. She questions whether he really dreamed of her, then slips out of his embrace. They exchange playful words, her movements light and teasing, as she avoids him before drawing close again, brushing the song into his ear and nipping at his earlobe. He insists she was beautiful in his dream, and she challenges him, her voice soft but edged with doubt. He reaffirms it, saying she is beautiful now.
related_events: Larch expresses affection upon waking, claiming he dreamed of Angela's beauty
Angela slips out of Larch's embrace after questioning the sincerity of his dream

name: Homer and the Pregnant Woman at the Orphanage Door
description: Homer walks up to the orphanage with a suitcase in hand just as a heavily pregnant woman arrives at the same time. They stand side by side in the dim morning light, waiting for someone to answer the door. The woman is crying. Homer reaches over and takes her hand. "Don't be frightened," he says. "Everyone is nice here." She sniffles, nods slightly. The door opens. Nurse Edna steps out, lets the woman in, and embraces Homer. Inside, a voice can be heard saying, "What could I do with him? He kept coming back!"
related_events: Homer and pregnant woman wait at orphanage door
Homer comforts pregnant woman by holding her hand

name: Nurse Edna Opens the Door
description: Nurse Edna opens the door of the orphanage. She lets the pregnant woman inside and embraces Homer warmly. The woman steps in, sniffling, her face damp with tears. Homer stands beside her, quiet and still, as the door closes behind them.
related_events: Nurse Edna opens door and welcomes woman and Homer

name: Angela and Edna Say Good-bye to Homer as Larch Watches
description: Angela and Edna, accompanied by COUPLE #2, walk away from the house, waving good-bye to two-year-old Homer. They make their way down the hill. Larch stands on the porch, watching them leave.
related_events: Angela and Edna wave good-bye to young Homer
Larch observes the family leaving down the hill

name: The Second Family Makes Homer Make Noises
description: Angela and Edna call and wave good-bye to two-year-old Homer as they leave with the second family. Larch stands on the porch, watching the group walk down the hill. As they depart, the second family unknowingly causes Homer to make sounds.
related_events: Second family elicits sounds from Homer

name: Buster and Homer Walk to the Incinerator
description: Buster and Homer tramp through the snow toward the incinerator. Homer carries a pail. Buster sniffs the air and says the old man smells of ether, and that he has seen him do it before. Homer replies that the old man uses ether because he is too tired to sleep. Buster says the smell is strong enough to put someone to sleep. Homer says doctors smell like ether. Buster points out that Homer is a doctor and does not smell like ether. Homer says he is not a doctor, that he has never been to medical school or even high school. Buster reminds him that he has studied with the old man for years. Homer repeats that he is not a doctor. Buster apologizes. They reach the incinerator, and Homer empties the pail into it while Buster watches.
related_events: Homer explains old man uses ether to stay awake
Buster challenges Homer's claim about doctors smelling like ether
Homer asserts he is not a doctor due to lack of formal education

name: Buster and Homer at the Incinerator
description: Buster and Homer walk through the snow toward the incinerator. Homer carries a pail. As they arrive, Homer empties the contents of the pail into the incinerator. Buster stands nearby and watches.
related_events: Buster and Homer walk through snow to incinerator
Buster observes Homer emptying pail into incinerator

name: Edna Kneels by the Frightened Girl
description: Edna kneels beside a terrified girl lying next to the incinerator. The children are nearby, chasing a ball. Edna speaks gently, telling the girl no one will hurt her, asking if she’s come to visit, if she’s had breakfast, and what her name is. The girl does not respond and flinches when Edna touches her forehead. Edna pulls her hand back, startled.
related_events: Edna kneels beside the frightened girl
Edna offers reassurance and asks the girl questions
Girl remains silent and cringes in fear
Edna touches the girl's forehead and reacts with alarm

name: Children Chasing a Ball Near the Incinerator
description: A group of children runs across the open area near the incinerator, laughing and calling out as they chase a bouncing ball. One child stumbles, another shouts in excitement, and they scramble together to retrieve it. The sound of their voices and footsteps fills the space, moving back and forth along the cracked ground beside the metal structure.
related_events: Children chase a ball near the incinerator

name: Homer and Larch Argue Over Abortion and Duty
description: The two doctors walk briskly down the hall, moving like professionals accustomed to the pace of the hospital. Larch asks if it's their first pregnancy, and Homer confirms it is—for both of them. Larch responds with a sarcastic remark about Homer wanting to handle the delivery. Homer, sounding weary, says again that he only meant he doesn't want to perform abortions, adding that he has no issue with Larch doing them. Larch presses him, asking how he can know how to help these women and still refuse when they have nowhere else to turn. Homer counters that the procedure is illegal and points out he never asked to learn it—Larch simply showed him. Larch replies that he could only teach what he knows, saying that in every life, a person has to be of use. The two part ways, each entering a different operating room. As Homer walks away, he mutters to himself, "Of use, of use, of use."
related_events: Doctors discuss ethical differences about abortion procedures
Homer expresses discomfort with learning abortion procedure
Larch justifies teaching Homer based on life purpose

name: Homer and Larch Enter Separate Operating Rooms
description: The two doctors walk down the hall in silence, then part ways, each entering a different operating room. As Homer opens the door and steps inside, he quietly repeats the words, 'of use, of use, of use,' under his breath.
related_events: Homer and Larch enter separate operating rooms
Homer repeats phrase 'of use' while entering operating room

name: Homer Carries the Pail and Sees What's Inside
description: Homer walks toward the incinerator carrying a white enamel pail. He stops and looks inside. His expression turns to disgust as he sees the contents. The sound of a song plays from an old phonograph.
related_events: Homer carries pail to incinerator
Homer discovers contents of pail

name: Larch's Confession
description: Homer carries a white enamel pail toward the incinerator. He pauses and looks inside, his face twisting into a look of disgust. Over this scene, Dr. Larch's voice is heard, speaking with sorrow: 'God forgive me. I have made an orphan by loving him too much. Homer Wells will belong to St. Cloud's, forever.' The image holds on Homer's expression as the song from an old phonograph begins to play.
related_events: Larch confesses guilt over making orphan

name: Homer Stares into the Pail as Phonograph Music Begins
description: Homer carries a white enamel pail to the incinerator. He looks inside the pail and stops. His face shows a look of disgust as he stares at its contents. The screen fades to black. From the darkness, a song begins to play on an old phonograph.
related_events: Old phonograph plays song

name: Larch's Benediction and the Returning Baby
description: Dr. Larch stands before the boys at the orphanage and speaks softly into the night, 'Good night, you Princes of Maine, you Kings of New England.' As he turns away, Nurse Edna steps forward with a couple and a baby. The adopting mother looks distressed, saying the baby never makes a sound. Larch glances at the child, then takes him into his arms. The baby lets out a happy squeal. The couple stares, silent and stunned, as Larch holds the child close.
related_events: Larch delivers benediction to the boys

name: Adopting Parents Return Baby Homer After He Doesn't Cry
description: Nurse Edna approaches Dr. Larch with an adopting couple and baby Homer. The adopting mother grows concerned, saying the baby never makes a sound. Dr. Larch looks at Homer quickly. The adopting father asks if they might see another baby. The mother hands Homer back to Dr. Larch. As soon as Homer is in Larch's arms, he lets out a happy squeal. The couple stares in silence. Homer remains at the orphanage.
related_events: Nurse Edna startles Larch with adopting couple and baby
Adopting mother expresses concern about baby's silence
Larch examines baby Homer upon parents' concern
Adopting father requests to see a different baby
Homer Wells is returned to the orphanage due to being too happy

name: Baby Homer Squeals in Larch's Arms
description: After the adopting mother hands baby Homer back to Dr. Larch, the infant lets out a happy squeal. The adopting parents stare in disbelief at the sudden sound.
related_events: Baby Homer squeals happily in Larch's arms
Adopting parents react in disbelief to baby's sudden sound

name: The Couple Stops to Look at Hazel
description: During breakfast, a couple walks around the dining area, moving from table to table as the children eat. They glance at the orphans, watching how they behave and appear. Curly eats a piece of pancake with careful fork movements, trying to show good manners. Angela and Edna attempt to guide the couple toward the older children, but the couple passes them by. They come to a halt near Hazel, standing still and staring at her, their attention fixed.
related_events: Would-be parents observe orphans during breakfast
Couple fixates on Hazel during breakfast

name: Angela and Edna Guide the Couple's Attention
description: As the couple walks among the children during breakfast, Angela and Edna move close and speak to them, gesturing toward the older children at the tables. They guide the couple along a slower path, pausing near the older kids as the couple glances around, taking in the scene.
related_events: Angela and Edna attempt to redirect couple's attention

name: Curly Eats with Elegance at Breakfast
description: During breakfast, Curly sits at the table with the other children as a visiting couple walks among them. He carefully lifts a piece of pancake with his fork and eats it with deliberate neatness, moving slowly and precisely. His posture remains upright, and his movements are controlled as he chews and sets the fork back down.
related_events: Curly demonstrates refined table manners

name: Homer Delivers Water and a Woman Asks Him to Touch Her Belly
description: Homer pushes a tray with glasses of water between hospital beds. A pregnant woman, visibly upset, stops him at her bedside. She asks if he is okay and if he needs anything. She tells him that no one else has ever touched her belly to feel the baby. She invites him to place his hand on her stomach. Homer does so. She then asks him to put his ear against her belly. He hesitates, then leans down and places his ear on her abdomen. She holds his head in place, pressing his face gently into her. Her eyes close. Homer lies there with his eyes open, motionless. A doctor appears in the doorway and watches silently. The woman tells Homer to stay exactly where he is, not to move.
related_events: Homer wheels water tray between hospital beds
Distraught pregnant woman asks Homer to touch her baby

name: Homer Touches and Listens to the Baby in the Pregnant Woman's Belly
description: Homer wheels a tray with glasses of water between the beds. A distraught pregnant woman stops him by her bed. She asks if he will touch her belly or put his ear to it to feel the baby. Homer hesitates, then touches her stomach. The woman urges him to listen, and he cautiously leans down, pressing his ear against her abdomen. She holds his head in place, pressing his face gently into her belly. Her eyes close as she tells him to stay, to remain right where he is. Homer remains still, his eyes wide open, as Dr. Larch watches from the doorway.
related_events: Homer touches pregnant woman's belly
Homer listens to baby by pressing ear to woman's belly

name: Woman Presses Homer's Head to Her Belly While Dr. Larch Watches
description: The distraught pregnant woman holds Homer's head firmly against her belly, pressing his face into her. She tells him to stay, repeating the words as if anchoring him in place. Homer remains still, his eyes wide. Dr. Larch appears in the doorway, watches the two of them without speaking, and stands there with a look of concern.
related_events: Distraught pregnant woman presses Homer's head against her belly
Dr. Larch observes Homer and the pregnant woman in the doorway

name: Buster Offers and Follows Despite Refusal
description: Homer walks through the dining room carrying a white enamel pail. Buster, a sixteen-year-old boy, notices him and calls out, offering to help. Homer shakes his head and keeps walking. Buster does not stop; he leaves the table of pastries and follows Homer anyway. Dr. Larch passes nearby, and Buster makes a face of disgust as he goes by.
related_events: Homer attracts Buster's attention while passing through the dining room
Buster offers to help Homer with his task
Homer refuses Buster's offer and continues walking
Buster follows Homer despite refusal

name: Buster Makes a Disgusted Face at Dr. Larch
description: Dr. Larch walks past Buster. As he passes by, Buster makes a face, showing disgust.
related_events: Buster makes a disgusted face as Dr. Larch passes by

name: Miss Titcomb Teaches Math in the Dining Room
description: In a corner of the dining room, Miss Titcomb stands by a wheeled blackboard covered in numbers, teaching math to a group of boys and girls who show little attention. The students fidget and glance away as she points to equations on the board. Nearby, the room remains active with other movements, but the lesson continues in its quiet corner.
related_events: Miss Titcomb teaches math to distracted students in the dining room

name: Dr. Larch Reads the Dog's Death and Says Good Night
description: Dr. Larch reads aloud from Oliver Twist, describing the death of Bill Sikes’s dog—the animal running along the parapet, howling, leaping for the dead man, missing, falling into a ditch, and dashing its brains out on a stone. The boys lie in their beds, listening in silence. Homer enters quietly, walks to his bed in the far corner, and begins to undress. Dr. Larch closes the book, turns off the lights, and stands in the open doorway. He speaks his nightly words: 'Good night, you Princes of Maine! You Kings of New England!' Then he closes the door, leaving the room in semi-darkness. Fuzzy, inside his breathing tent, asks why Dr. Larch does that every night. Curly suggests it’s to scare them. Copperfield calls him a jerk. Steerforth says Dr. Larch loves them. Fuzzy still wonders why. Buster says it’s because they like it. The boys are quiet, and in the dimness, they all seem to agree.
related_events: Dr. Larch reads death scene of Bill Sike's dog to boys
Dr. Larch turns off lights and delivers bedtime benediction

name: Homer Returns During Bedtime Reading
description: Homer enters the dormitory quietly while Dr. Larch is reading. The other boys lie in their beds, listening. Homer walks to his bed in the far corner and begins to undress, settling in as the story continues.
related_events: Homer enters dormitory and begins undressing

name: Boys Discuss Dr. Larch's Bedtime Reading
description: After Dr. Larch turned off the lights and closed the door, a young boy ran from his bed to Homer's, climbing in beside him. From inside his breathing tent, Fuzzy asked why Dr. Larch read that story every night. Curly suggested it was to scare them. Copperfield called him a jerk. Steerforth said Dr. Larch loved them. Fuzzy asked again why he did it, and Buster replied that he did it because they liked it. The boys fell silent, and in the dimness, they all seemed to agree.
related_events: Young boy runs into Homer's bed and questions Dr. Larch's nightly reading
Boys exchange thoughts on Dr. Larch's bedtime ritual
Boys silently agree on reason for Dr. Larch's bedtime reading

name: Homer Finds Curly with a Suitcase in the Corridor
description: Homer sees Curly standing alone by a window in the corridor, a suitcase at his side. He greets him and asks if he is going somewhere. Curly shakes his head and says he thought they might take him, but Homer replies that they wanted a girl. Curly says nobody ever wants him. Homer embraces him, lifts him up, and takes the suitcase. As he carries Curly away down the corridor, he tells him he’s one of the best and that they couldn’t let just anyone take him. Curly recalls that Dr. Larch wouldn’t let just anyone take any of them. Homer assures him that nobody special enough has asked for him, but someone did ask—only the right people can have him. Homer then enters the boys’ bunk room with Curly and the suitcase, leaving the corridor empty.
related_events: Homer greets Curly in the corridor

name: Curly Questions If Anyone Has Asked for Him
description: Homer sees Curly standing alone by a window in the corridor with a suitcase at his side. He greets him, asking if he is going somewhere. Curly shakes his head and says he thought they might take him. Homer reminds him that the people who came were looking for a girl. Curly says no one ever wants him. Homer hugs him and lifts him up, then picks up the suitcase and carries it as he walks down the corridor with Curly. He tells Curly he is one of the best and that they couldn’t let just anyone take him. Curly says Dr. Larch wouldn’t let just anyone take any of them. After a pause, Curly asks if anyone has asked for him. Homer says no one special enough. Curly asks if someone did ask, and Homer replies that only the right people can have him. Homer then enters the boys’ bunk room still carrying Curly and the suitcase, leaving the corridor empty.
related_events: Curly expresses feeling unwanted
Curly questions whether anyone has asked for him

name: Homer Lifts Curly and Takes His Suitcase
description: Homer finds Curly standing alone by a window in the corridor, a suitcase at his side. He greets him, and Curly says he thought they might take him, but adds that nobody ever wants him. Homer embraces Curly, lifts him up, and picks up the suitcase. He tells Curly he’s one of the best and that they couldn’t let just anyone take him. Curly remembers that Dr. Larch wouldn’t let just anyone take any of them. Homer says no one special enough has asked for Curly, but that only the right people can have him. Then Homer carries Curly and his suitcase into the boys’ bunk room, leaving the corridor empty.
related_events: Homer lifts Curly and takes his suitcase
Homer reassures Curly about his value
Homer clarifies that only the right people can adopt Curly

name: Homer Takes Curly to the Bunk Room
description: Homer lifts Curly into his arms, picks up the suitcase from the floor, and carries both into the boys' bunk room. The corridor is left empty behind them.
related_events: Homer carries Curly into the boys' bunk room

name: Homer Delivers Carla's Baby and Calms Her After Birth
description: Homer delivers Carla's baby. The newborn cries as Edna holds him. Homer tells Carla she did well and that everything is fine. Carla, still on the bed, gasps for breath and says she doesn’t want to see the baby or know the sex. Edna comforts her, saying she doesn’t have to. Homer continues to reassure her. Larch enters, looks at the baby, and says, 'He's a big boy!' Carla suddenly says she wants to see the child. Edna shows her the baby. Carla looks at him, then turns away. Larch whispers to Homer, asking him to check on Dorothy.
related_events: Homer delivers baby CARLA
Homer reassures Carla after childbirth
Newborn baby screams in Edna's arms

name: Carla Changes Her Mind About Seeing the Baby
description: Carla lies on the delivery table, breathing heavily after giving birth. She tells Homer and Edna she does not want to see the baby or know its sex. Edna holds the crying newborn, comforting Carla. Larch enters, looks at the baby, and says, 'He's a big boy!' Carla suddenly says, 'Let me see him, for Christ's sake—I wanna see him.' Edna brings the baby closer, and Carla looks at the infant. After a moment, she turns her face away.
related_events: Carla refuses to see or know about the baby
Carla requests to see her newborn baby
Edna shows newborn baby to Carla who then turns away

name: Larch Checks the Newborn and Sends Homer to Dorothy
description: Dr. Larch steps into the delivery room and looks at the newborn. He remarks that the baby is a big boy. Carla, who had earlier refused to see the child, suddenly wants to see him. Edna shows her the baby, and Carla stares before turning away. Larch leans in and quietly tells Homer to go check on Dorothy.
related_events: Larch enters delivery room and observes newborn baby
Larch whispers request to Homer about Dorothy

name: Edna Comforts Carla After Childbirth
description: After the baby is born, Carla pants heavily, overwhelmed. Homer reassures her, telling her she did well and that everything is fine. Carla says she doesn’t want to see the baby and doesn’t want to know its sex. Edna holds the newborn, who is crying, and tells Carla she doesn’t have to look, that it’s all right. She assures Carla that both she and the baby will be okay. Carla repeats that she doesn’t want to know anything about the baby. Moments later, she changes her mind and asks to see the child. Edna shows her the baby. Carla looks at it, then turns away.
related_events: Edna comforts Carla during postpartum moment

name: Dr. Larch Takes Ether at St. Cloud's
description: In the dispensary at St. Cloud's, Maine, in March 1943, Dr. Larch sits on a bed, holding a bottle of ether in one hand and a cone over his mouth and nose with the other. The phonograph plays a song as he begins to inhale the ether. His hand relaxes, the cone slips from his face, and he dozes off. Moments later, he stirs, opens his eyes, and reaches for the cone. He places it back over his nose and mouth, then drips more ether from the bottle onto the gauze covering the cone. Around him, the room remains still—the medical cabinets, the photographs on the walls, the hospital curtain drawn around the bed. Homer enters, stands quietly for a moment, watching, then turns and walks back into the corridor.
related_events: Dr. Larch inhales ether using a cone apparatus
Dr. Larch dozes off and drops the ether cone
Dr. Larch wakes up and repositions the ether cone

name: Dr. Larch in the Dispensary
description: The camera moves across the room, showing the dispensary where Dr. Larch lives. Shelves hold glass-encased medical supplies. Old photographs of St. Cloud's line the walls. A hospital curtain on casters separates a bed where Larch lies, using ether. A record turns on a phonograph. Larch holds the ether bottle in one hand and a cone over his face with the other. As he dozes, the cone slips away and falls. He wakes, places it back over his nose and mouth, and drips more ether onto the gauze. Homer enters, stands still for a moment, watching. Then he turns and walks out into the corridor.
related_events: Camera pans across the dispensary and living quarters

name: Homer Watches Larch and Leaves
description: Homer enters the dispensary where Dr. Larch lies on the ether-bed, the cone over his face, a bottle of ether in his hand. The room is lined with glass-encased medical cabinets and old photographs of St. Cloud's. A record turns on the phonograph. Larch dozes, the cone slips from his face, and he stirs, replacing it and dripping more ether onto the gauze. Homer stands still, watching. After a moment, he turns and walks back into the corridor.
related_events: Homer enters the room and observes Dr. Larch uneasily
Homer turns around and leaves the room

name: Larch and Homer Place Fuzzy in the Humidified Tent
description: Dr. Larch and Homer assemble a humidified tent over a small hospital bed on wheels, connecting the humidifier to a car battery. Larch lifts Fuzzy from in front of the phonograph and zips him into the tent. Fuzzy smiles inside. Soon after, he begins to cough and wheeze, his breaths labored. Homer leans down and peers through a hole near the zipper. Mary Agnes enters the room, sticks out her tongue, and tells Homer it might have been bitten while kissing someone. Homer examines it and says she likely bit it herself, perhaps in her sleep. Mary Agnes suggests she might have been dreaming of kissing someone. Homer does not respond. He wheels Fuzzy into the hallway, saying, "Story time, Fuzzy!"
related_events: Larch and Homer construct a humidified tent for Fuzzy
Larch moves Fuzzy into the breathing tent
Fuzzy smiles after being placed in the breathing tent
Fuzzy begins coughing and wheezing inside the breathing tent

name: Larch and Homer Prepare the Humidified Tent for Fuzzy
description: Fuzzy, a small, pale six-year-old who resembles an embryo, listens to a recording on Larch's phonograph, his head tilted toward the giant ear of the machine. Nearby, Dr. Larch and Homer assemble a humidified tent over a small hospital bed on wheels, powering the humidifier with a car battery. As they work, Larch remarks on how often premature babies of alcoholic mothers fall ill, citing Fuzzy as an example. He notes that Fuzzy is constantly battling bronchitis and dismisses the lack of medical literature on the subject, insisting that real experience matters more than published studies. Homer questions whether Fuzzy might simply be underdeveloped, but Larch counters by pointing to the severity of the boy’s recurring infections. Larch then lifts Fuzzy from the phonograph and zips him into the tent. Fuzzy smiles. As Larch leaves, Mary Agnes enters the dispensary, sticks her tongue out at Homer, and claims she might have bitten it while dreaming of kissing someone. Homer examines her tongue, tells her she did it herself, and wheels Fuzzy into the hallway, saying, "Story time, Fuzzy." Fuzzy begins to cough and wheeze inside the tent.
related_events: Larch discusses Fuzzy's medical condition with Homer
Fuzzy listens to a phonograph recording

name: Mary Agnes Shows Her Bitten Tongue
description: Mary Agnes enters the dispensary and smiles at Homer before sticking her tongue out. Homer looks at her without expression. She speaks with difficulty, pointing to her tongue, and says she doesn’t remember biting it. Homer leans in to examine it and tells her it looks like she did it herself, maybe in her sleep. She suggests someone might have bitten her while kissing, but Homer doesn’t respond. She adds that she must have been dreaming of kissing someone. Homer remains silent, then wheels Fuzzy’s bed out of the room, saying it’s time for a story.
related_events: Mary Agnes shows her bitten tongue to Homer

name: Homer Takes Fuzzy to Story Time
description: After placing Fuzzy inside the breathing tent and checking on him, Homer wheels the small hospital bed into the hallway. As he pushes the bed, he announces it is time for a story. Mary Agnes, standing nearby, sticks her tongue out at him, but Homer does not respond. Fuzzy coughs softly, his breathing still labored, as the humidifier hums from the car battery powering it.
related_events: Homer wheels Fuzzy into the hallway for story time

name: Larch and Homer Examine Dorothy's Uterus
description: Larch and Homer stand over a basin containing Dorothy's uterus, studying the tissue in silence. There are no visible wounds, but the organ is disintegrating—stitches pull through it like paper. Homer suggests the damage resembles scurvy. Larch scoffs, pointing out that scurvy comes from a lack of fresh food, not something a prostitute like Dorothy would typically suffer. Angela interjects, confirming Dorothy's profession. Homer asks if anyone checked her purse. Larch, frustrated, says he’s already searched everywhere. Angela hands Larch a small bottle of brown liquid labeled French Lunar Solution. Larch sniffs it, disgusted. He tastes a drop and spits, identifying it as oil of tansy. He explains that tansy prevents the intestines from absorbing Vitamin C, leading to scurvy. Homer acknowledges the connection. Larch praises him, then turns to Angela, telling her to stay with Dorothy—she’s in danger. As Homer moves to leave, Larch gestures to the basin. Homer hesitates, then picks it up and pours the contents into a white enamel pail.
related_events: Larch and Homer examine Dorothy's uterus after failed abortion
Homer compares symptoms to scurvy
Larch expresses frustration after searching for medical clues

name: Larch Identifies the Poison in Dorothy's Bottle
description: Angela hands Larch a bottle of brown liquid labeled French Lunar Solution, which she found in Dorothy's purse. Larch wrinkles his nose at the strong odor. He dips his finger into the liquid, touches it to his tongue, and immediately spits. He identifies the substance as oil of tansy. He explains that ingesting it prevents the intestines from absorbing Vitamin C, leading to scurvy. Homer recognizes the connection to Dorothy’s condition, and Larch acknowledges his correct assumption.
related_events: Angela provides bottle of French Lunar Solution to Larch
Larch reacts to the odor and contents of French Lunar Solution
Larch tastes French Lunar Solution and identifies oil of tansy
Larch explains oil of tansy causes scurvy

name: Angela Reveals Dorothy's Profession and the Bottle is Identified
description: Angela states that Dorothy is a prostitute. Homer asks Angela if she looked in Dorothy's purse. Angela retrieves a bottle of brown liquid and hands it to Larch, telling him it is called French Lunar Solution and that it claims to restore monthly regularity. Larch tastes a drop, spits it out, and identifies the substance as oil of tansy. He explains that it prevents the intestines from absorbing Vitamin C, leading to scurvy. Larch then tells Angela to keep an eye on Dorothy, saying she is in trouble.
related_events: Angela reveals Dorothy's profession as a prostitute
Homer asks Angela if she checked Dorothy's purse
Larch instructs Angela to monitor Dorothy's condition

name: Homer Disposes of the Uterine Tissue
description: As Homer turned to leave, Larch stopped him and pointed to the basin holding Dorothy's uterine tissue. Homer paused, visibly annoyed, then picked up the basin and poured its contents into a white enamel pail.
related_events: Larch instructs Homer to dispose of uterine contents
Homer disposes of uterine contents in enamel pail

name: Larch and Angela Prepare Dorothy for Ether
description: Larch holds the ether cone and asks Dorothy if she has ever had ether before. She replies that she had it once when her appendix was removed. Angela looks for a scar on Dorothy’s abdomen but finds none, saying no one has touched her appendix. Dorothy hesitates, recalling that the ether made her sick during the previous procedure. Larch assures her it won’t happen this time, explaining he will administer it in small drops. Dorothy says she cannot pay, and Larch tells her that any future donation to the orphanage would be appreciated, though Angela adds it is only if she can afford it. Larch then instructs Dorothy to try to think of nothing. Angela places the cone over Dorothy’s mouth and nose, and Larch begins dripping ether onto it. From the other operating room, the cry of a newborn echoes.
related_events: Dorothy recalls previous experience with ether
Angela searches for surgical scar on Dorothy
Larch reassures Dorothy about ether administration

name: Dorothy's Payment Concern and Larch's Offer
description: Dorothy says she cannot pay for the procedure, having no money. Larch tells her that if she ever has any money in the future, a donation to the orphanage would be appreciated. Angela adds that it’s only if she can afford it. Dorothy lies on the table as Larch holds the ether bottle, telling her to try to think of nothing. Angela places the cone over Dorothy’s mouth and nose, and Larch begins dripping ether onto it. The cry of a newborn echoes from the other operating room.
related_events: Dorothy expresses inability to pay for the procedure
Larch requests future donation to the orphanage

name: Larch and Angela Administer Ether to Dorothy
description: Larch holds the ether bottle while Angela places the cone over Dorothy's mouth and nose. Larch drips ether onto the cone, one drop at a time. Across the hall, a newborn cries. Dorothy lies still as the ether takes effect.
related_events: Angela and Larch administer ether to Dorothy
Larch and Angela prepare ether for Dorothy

name: Newborn's Cry During Dorothy's Procedure
description: As Angela placed the cone over Dorothy's mouth and nose, and Larch began dripping ether onto it, a newborn's cry rang out from the operating room next door. The sound filled the space, sharp and sudden, as the clinic continued its work on both sides of the wall.
related_events: Newborn cries in the operating room

name: Edna Defends Hazel's Adoption Day
description: Hazel stands clutching a cardboard suitcase and a tattered rag doll as Edna fusses over her. Mary Agnes, sitting on a bed, says that if people want to adopt one of them, they should take the oldest first. Edna interrupts, urging Mary Agnes not to make Hazel feel sad because it is her special day. Mary Agnes replies that Hazel is practically the youngest and should be the last to leave. Clara adds that at least Hazel can talk, unlike the babies they usually take. Mary Agnes says they take babies so they never have to tell them they were orphans. Hazel begins to cry and says she is not a baby. Mary Agnes warns her that if she cries, they will send her back. Edna contradicts her, saying that is not true, and tells Hazel she can cry as much as she wants.
related_events: Mary Agnes expresses objection to adoption order
Edna defends Hazel's special day
Mary Agnes argues Hazel should be last to leave

name: Hazel Cries on Her Adoption Day
description: Clara remarks that adoptive parents usually take the babies because they can talk, unlike the younger children. Mary Agnes responds that people take babies so they never have to tell them they were orphans. Hazel begins to cry. Mary Agnes tells her that if she cries, the family will send her back, saying it happened to her before. Edna interrupts, insisting Mary Agnes is wrong, and tells Hazel she can cry if she wants to. Hazel cries harder.
related_events: Clara comments on adopters preferring non-verbal children
Hazel begins to cry upon hearing Mary Agnes's claim about adoptive parents

name: Hazel's Adoption Day
description: Hazel clutches a cardboard suitcase and a tattered rag doll as Edna fusses over her. Mary Agnes, sitting on a bed, says that if people want to adopt one of them, they should take the oldest first. Edna hushes her, reminding her it’s Hazel’s special day. Mary Agnes insists Hazel is practically the youngest and should be the last to leave. Clara remarks that at least Hazel can talk, since they usually take the babies. Mary Agnes adds that they take babies so they never have to tell them they were orphans. Hazel begins to cry. Mary Agnes tells her that if she cries, they’ll send her back. Edna contradicts her, saying that’s not true. Hazel cries harder. Mary Agnes says that’s what happened to her—she was sent back. Edna replies that Mary Agnes wanted to come back, which is why she cried, then turns to Hazel and tells her she can cry if she feels like it, that she can cry as much as she wants.
related_events: Mary Agnes warns Hazel that crying will result in being sent back
Mary Agnes reveals that she was sent back after crying during her adoption
Edna reframes Mary Agnes's return as a desire to come back rather than rejection
Edna reassures Hazel that she can cry if she wants to

name: Edna Fusses Over Hazel Before She Leaves
description: Edna tends to Hazel, who stands clutching a cardboard suitcase and a tattered rag doll. Her hands move with small adjustments—smoothing Hazel’s dress, brushing her hair—while Hazel begins to cry. The room is quiet except for her soft sobs. Mary Agnes sits on the bed, watching. Clara remains nearby, her words hanging in the air. Edna tells Hazel she can cry as much as she wants.
related_events: Edna fusses over Hazel as she prepares to leave

name: Larch and Homer Examine the Newborns
description: Larch and Homer move from crib to crib, checking the newborns' reflexes, grips, eyes, ears, and throats. They pause at each bed, reviewing records and making quiet observations. A nurse or assistant occasionally hands them a tool or adjusts a blanket. The room is quiet except for the soft sounds of infants stirring and the doctors' murmured notes.
related_events: Doctors examine newborn babies' physical conditions

name: Angela Informs Larch of the Waiting Couple
description: Angela appears in the doorway and tells Larch that the adopting couple is waiting in his office. Larch responds with irritation, muttering, "Life is waiting," before turning back to the babies.
related_events: Angela informs Larch about the adopting couple
Larch expresses irritation about life's urgency

name: Larch and Homer Name an Unnamed Baby
description: Larch looks at the baby's record attached to the bed and asks where the name sheet is. Homer replies that no one has named this baby yet. Larch declares it's his turn to name the child and touches the baby's forehead, announcing the name Little Dorrit. The baby begins to cry. Homer says the baby doesn't like it and points out the child is a boy. Larch challenges whether a boy can't be named Dorrit, then tells Homer to name the baby instead. Homer mimics pointing a gun with his finger, touches the baby's forehead, and declares the name Little Wilbur. Larch expresses dislike for the 'Little' part, so Homer writes the name as just Wilbur. Larch comments that they haven't had a baby named Wilbur in about a year, adding that they used to have dozens. Before they can continue, Copperfield runs into the room, excitedly announcing that the adopting couple has picked Hazel.
related_events: Larch searches for the baby's name sheet
Homer reveals unnamed baby

name: Larch Names the Baby Little Dorrit
description: Larch looks at the baby's record and asks for the name sheet. Homer replies that no one has named this baby yet. Larch says it's his turn and touches the infant's forehead with his index finger, declaring, 'Henceforth you shall be... Little Dorrit!' The baby immediately begins to cry.
related_events: Larch names the unnamed baby Little Dorrit
Baby begins to cry after being named

name: Homer Names the Baby Wilbur
description: Homer pointed his finger at the baby's forehead and declared, 'Henceforth you shall be... Little Wilbur.' Larch expressed his dislike for the 'Little' prefix. Homer then revised the name, saying, 'Okay, he's just a Wilbur then,' and wrote the name on the baby's record.
related_events: Homer suggests naming the baby Little Wilbur
Homer changes the baby's name to Wilbur

name: Copperfield Interrupts the Naming
description: Copperfield runs into the room, calling out that the adopting couple has picked Hazel. He says they chose her, calling them idiots. The announcement cuts off Larch and Homer, who had been naming a newborn baby moments before.
related_events: Copperfield announces Hazel's selection by the adopting couple

name: Homer and Buster at the Train Station
description: Homer and Buster sit on a loading cart at the train station as a train approaches. The train slows and stops, its windows filled with soldiers. A woman, no longer pregnant, stands waiting, her face blank, as the stationmaster eyes her disapprovingly. Buster kicks a rock and asks Homer if he ever thinks about leaving to find his parents. Homer says he does think about leaving, but not to find them—he sees Dr. Larch, Nurse Edna, and Nurse Angela as his real parents because they did what parents are supposed to do. Buster says he sometimes wishes he could meet his own parents, just to show them he can cook and drive a truck. Homer laughs and agrees he cooks well and drives better than he does. Then Buster admits, quietly, that sometimes he wants to meet them so he can kill them. He immediately looks ashamed and insists he would never do it, and Homer tells him he knows. Nearby, Mary Agnes walks past the train, trying to look grown and composed. A soldier leans out and tugs her hair. She spits at him, then at all the others as they roll up their windows. She shouts after them. Buster says he thinks Mary Agnes could kill someone. Homer watches her and says she’s just an emotional girl. Buster asks why she’s so upset. Homer shrugs and says she was left here, like the rest of them. The camera lingers on Homer’s face.
related_events: Homer and Buster sit on loading cart as train approaches
Buster reveals conflicting feelings about meeting his biological parents
Homer expresses loyalty to Dr. Larch and nurses as parental figures
Buster apologizes for expressing violent thought about his parents

name: Mary Agnes Spits at Soldiers After Hair Tug
description: The train came to a stop, soldiers leaning out the windows. One of them reached out and gently tugged on Mary Agnes's hair as she walked past. She turned, spat at him, then moved along the train spitting at all the soldiers. Shouting after them, she hurled insults as they rolled up the windows to shut her out.
related_events: Train stops with soldiers leaning out windows
Soldier gently tugs on Mary Agnes's hair
Mary Agnes spits at soldier in response to harassment
Soldiers roll up train windows to block Mary Agnes's abuse

name: Homer and Buster Watch Mary Agnes Confront the Soldiers
description: As the train comes to a stop, soldiers lean out of the windows, watching the people on the platform. One of them reaches out and tugs gently on Mary Agnes's hair as she walks past. She turns, spits at him, then spits at the others as she moves down the line. The soldiers quickly roll up their windows. Homer and Buster, sitting on a loading cart nearby, watch in silence. Buster says he thinks Mary Agnes could kill someone. Homer shakes his head, calling her an emotional girl. Buster asks what she’s so upset about. Homer shrugs and says she was left here, just like the rest of them.
related_events: Homer and Buster comment on Mary Agnes's emotional state

name: The Woman Leaves St. Cloud's
description: A woman stands at the train station, her face blank and heavy with sorrow, no longer pregnant. She waits in silence as the train approaches, carrying her away from St. Cloud's. The stationmaster fixes her with a hard, disapproving look. The train slows to a stop, soldiers leaning out of the windows. Nearby, Homer and Buster sit on a loading cart, watching. The woman does not speak or react. She steps aboard the train without a glance back.
related_events: Distraught woman waits for train after leaving St. Cloud's without her baby
Stationmaster gives disapproving look to departing woman

name: Mary Agnes Leads Snowball Ambush Until Boys Strike Back
description: Mary Agnes and the girls round the corner of the orphanage, pulling a sled piled with snowballs. Mary Agnes points and gives instructions, assigning Buster to herself and directing Clara and Hazel to target Copperfield and Curly, warning them to leave Fuzzy alone. Before they can act, the boys burst forward in a surprise attack. Buster hurls two snowballs that strike Mary Agnes and Clara. Mary Agnes tackles Buster, shoving his head repeatedly into the snow. Copperfield flees in fear. Curly throws a snowball that misses, then stumbles and overturns the sled as Clara and Hazel tackle him to the ground. Fuzzy drops his snowball and runs in circles, coughing uncontrollably, until Nurse Edna bursts out of the orphanage door and shouts for them to stop.
related_events: Girls prepare for snowball fight led by Mary Agnes
Boys launch surprise attack in snowball fight

name: Mary Agnes Subdues Buster, Clara and Hazel Tackle Curly
description: Buster throws two snowballs that strike Mary Agnes and Clara. Mary Agnes lunges at Buster, overpowers him, and shoves his head repeatedly into the snow. Curly hurls a snowball but misses, then stumbles and knocks over the sled piled with snowballs. Clara and Hazel rush forward and tackle Curly, bringing him to the ground.
related_events: Buster hits Mary Agnes and Clara with snowballs
Mary Agnes subdues Buster by shoving his head in snow
Curly misses throw and sled is overturned
Clara and Hazel tackle Curly to the ground

name: Nurse Edna Stops the Snowball Fight
description: Nurse Edna bursts out of the orphanage door as the children scramble in the snow. She shouts for them to stop fighting and demands they share the snowballs. Buster spits out snow and protests that the girls stole the snowballs from the boys. Nearby, Fuzzy drops his snowball, runs in circles while coughing and gasping for breath. Nurse Edna sees him struggling and immediately orders him to go to the shower. The children quiet down, brushing snow off their clothes, as a new couple begins walking up the hill toward the orphanage.
related_events: Nurse Edna emerges angrily from orphanage door
Nurse Edna orders children to stop fighting and share snowballs
Buster claims snowballs belong to boys and were stolen by girls
Fuzzy shows signs of respiratory distress after running
Fuzzy drops snowball and runs while coughing

name: Buster and Mary Agnes Blame Each Other After Snowball Fight
description: After the snowball fight, Buster spits out snow and shouts that the snowballs were theirs, accusing the girls of stealing them. Mary Agnes stands firm, brushing snow from her sleeves, and says the boys attacked them just like the Japs. The other children watch quietly, catching their breath as the argument unfolds.
related_events: Buster claims snowballs belong to boys and were stolen by girls
Mary Agnes compares boys' attack to Japanese assault

name: The Arrival of the New Couple
description: A new couple walks up the hill toward the orphanage. The children immediately stop their snowball fight, brushing snow off their clothes and hair, straightening themselves out. Curly frantically tries to smooth his hair and adjust his coat, standing up straight as the couple approaches. Mary Agnes watches them without fixing her appearance, then leans toward Clara and Hazel and whispers, 'I know the type—they'll take one of the babies.'
related_events: New couple arrives at orphanage prompting children to tidy up
Curly tries to appear attractive to visiting couple
Mary Agnes decides visiting couple will adopt a baby

name: The Orphans Watch King Kong
description: The orphans sit in the darkened room, eyes fixed on the screen as King Kong carries Fay Wray into the cave. Their faces flicker in the projector light, rapt and wide-eyed. Fuzzy points at the screen, coughing between words. "He thinks she's his *mother*!" he says. Copperfield shakes his head. "He doesn't think she's his mother, Fuzzy." "He does so!" Fuzzy insists. "He *loves* her!" Carla frowns. "How could she be his *mother*?" The film snaps, the image dissolving into white light. A chorus of groans rises from the children. "Kong! Kong!" they chant. Fuzzy keeps coughing as Dr. Larch fumbles with the projector, squinting at the broken film. Angela turns on the light. Homer walks up from the front row. Larch turns to him. "I thought you took care of this. It always breaks in the same place. It's your splice, isn't it?" "It's *your* splice!" Homer snaps. "You blame me for everything!" Larch lets go of the film. "Angela, we need a new movie, a new projector, a new typewriter—*that's* what they should replace around here!" Edna steps in. "We have a delivery. Imminent, in my estimation..." Larch turns to Homer. "Homer, would you get this one?" Homer shifts his weight, standing still. "She's a patient, right? She should see a doctor." Larch looks at him. "Homer, you are a skilled and gifted surgeon. You have near-perfect obstetrical and gynecological procedure." Homer hesitates. "I just mean I'd rather fix the movie. Tonight." Larch exhales. "Sure. Okay. You splice. I'll deliver."
related_events: Orphans watch King Kong film scene with Fay Wray
Fuzzy claims King Kong believes Fay Wray is his mother

name: The Film Breaks and the Orphans Chant for Kong
description: The movie suddenly stops playing, the image freezing on the screen. A wave of groans and cries rises from the orphans, their faces lit with frustration. They begin chanting in unison, 'Kong! Kong!', their voices filling the room. Angela stands and flips the light switch, flooding the space with brightness. Dr. Larch leans over the projector, squinting at the tangled film, while the orphans continue to call out, their attention now fixed on the broken machine and the adults trying to fix it.
related_events: Film projector breaks during screening
Orphans chant 'Kong!' in disappointment
Angela turns on lights during projector repair

name: Larch and Homer Argue Over the Broken Film
description: The film snaps during the screening, plunging the room into darkness as the orphans cry out in disappointment. Fuzzy continues to cough while Larch fumbles with the projector, squinting at the broken strip of film. Angela turns on the light. The children begin chanting, "Kong! Kong!" Larch calls for Homer, who gets up from his seat and walks to the front. Larch accuses him of making a poor splice, saying it always breaks in the same place. Homer snaps back, insisting the splice was Larch’s own work and that he’s being blamed for everything. For a moment, they stand face to face, tension hanging between them, before Larch abruptly lets go of the film and turns away.
related_events: Dr. Larch confronts Homer about faulty film splice

name: Larch Learns of the Board's Plans During Movie Night
description: While the orphans watch King Kong, their faces lit by the flickering screen, Dr. Larch sits beside the projector with a letter in hand. He reads it silently, then shakes it at Angela, whispering fiercely that the Board of Trustees wants to replace him. Angela replies in a hushed tone that they only want him to hire new help. Larch scoffs, saying he doesn’t need new people—what the orphanage needs are new things: a movie projector, a typewriter. The film snaps, plunging the room into darkness as the orphans cry out in protest. Fuzzy coughs loudly. Larch fumbles with the broken reel as Angela turns on the light. The children chant, "Kong! Kong!" Larch calls for Homer, who comes forward. Larch accuses him of botching the splice, but Homer snaps back that it was Larch’s own work. They glare at each other until Edna enters and announces a delivery is imminent. Larch turns to Homer and asks him to handle it. Homer hesitates, shifting his weight, and says the patient should see a doctor. Larch tells him he is a skilled surgeon, capable in obstetrics and gynecology. Homer remains still, saying he’d rather fix the movie tonight. Larch pauses, then agrees. He will deliver. Homer will splice the film. The tension eases, but uneasily.
related_events: Dr. Larch reveals Board of Trustees wants to replace him

name: Homer Refuses to Assist with Delivery
description: Edna enters the room and announces that a patient is about to go into labor, saying the delivery is imminent. Dr. Larch turns to Homer and asks him to handle the delivery. Homer hesitates, then refuses, saying the patient should see a doctor. He adds that he would rather fix the broken film that has stopped playing. The orphans are still chanting for King Kong, and the projector light casts shadows on the wall. Dr. Larch tells Homer he is a skilled and gifted surgeon, pointing out his experience with obstetrical and gynecological procedures. Homer stands his ground, shifting his weight but not moving toward the door. Dr. Larch looks at him with disappointment, then agrees to handle the delivery himself. He tells Homer to fix the film instead. Homer walks back to the projector as Larch leaves the room.
related_events: Edna announces an imminent patient delivery
Homer refuses to assist with patient delivery
Dr. Larch praises Homer's surgical skills during confrontation

name: Larch Takes Over the Delivery
description: After Homer refuses to assist with the patient delivery, Dr. Larch turns to him and says he will handle it himself. He steps away from the projector, visibly disappointed, and walks out to attend to the delivery. Homer remains behind, standing near the broken film as the orphans continue to chant for King Kong.
related_events: Dr. Larch decides to handle delivery after Homer refuses

name: Homer Reads 'David Copperfield' to the Boys
description: The boys climb into bed as Homer adjusts Fuzzy's breathing tent. Fuzzy asks if King Kong thinks the woman is his mother. Homer says yes, that’s what Kong thinks. Fuzzy says that’s why Kong loves her, and Homer agrees. Larch enters, exchanges a look with Homer, and takes over adjusting the tent. Homer sits down with 'David Copperfield' and begins to read aloud. He reads the opening lines: 'Whether I shall turn out to be the hero of my own life, or whether that station will be held by anybody else, these pages must show.' He continues, 'I was a posthumous child. My father's eyes had closed upon the light of this world six months, when mine opened on it.' Fuzzy whispers to Larch, asking if the boy’s father is dead. Larch whispers back that he is. Fuzzy then asks if Larch’s father is dead too. Larch nods and says cirrhosis, a disease of the liver, killed him. Fuzzy asks if liver killed him, and Larch clarifies that alcohol killed him—he drank himself to death. Fuzzy wants to know if Larch knew his father. Larch says barely, and it hardly mattered. Fuzzy asks if Larch knew his mother better. Larch nods and says she’s dead now, too, and that she was a nanny. Fuzzy asks what a nanny does. Larch says she looks after other people's children.
